auditGaps.gap: Front and three-quarter: each fan wing is a rounded pad with a beaded, knobbed rim, lumps on its face and crinkled cup-wall seams; the cup is a thick ring around a hole (the far ear reads as a toothed wreath in three-quarter) and the inner tufts are stiff white leaf blades covering under half the cup, not a soft fur mass with a pale fluffy tuft.

Side and top: the ear seen from the side is a tall oval shell split by a slit lined with tooth-like beads (a clam or flytrap) with no pale inner cup showing; from above the fan is still a thin flat tray with no forward cup depth.

Front outline: the fan's top edge runs level tip to tip so the V tilt is gone, the tips are rounded ends rather than up-flared points, and the span is too wide (R03.1 1.043, R01.1 IoU .874; full width at .02 is .501 against .280).

Side and three-quarter: the eye in profile is a wedge tapering to a point with the iris a dark sliver at its front edge; in three-quarter the far eye is a pinched teardrop with a kinked lid and a small centred pupil, so the face looks worried.

Back and rear oblique: the head dome is a smooth disc bounded by two straight vertical cut lines through the fan, the wings carry knobs and a peg fringe on the lower edge, and the inner lower fan edge drops beside the head base so it no longer narrows into the neck (R01.6 1.329, R04.1 IoU .870).
All views: a lumpy, beaded head on a completely smooth bare body with no cheek, chest or limb masses; under the fur ruling this mostly follows from smoothing the fan to the body's level.
Front: near-round white eye discs with small pupils dead centre give a stare; the sheet has tall ovals with a heavier upper lid and a large iris glancing to one side.

Front: the crown sits level with the fan top and carries a row of small knobs instead of rising between the ear roots, and the lower face is broad with cheek bulges at the mouth line instead of tapering to a small rounded chin.

Front and back: square shoulders with deltoid caps over a pinched waist read as an athletic hourglass, and from behind the upper back is a disc framed by dark notches at the shoulder corners (posed trunk IoU .853).

Side: the top of the upper arm is a pale flat-topped cap with a hard upper edge so the shoulder juts as a box, and a cuff band rings the wrist; these are the two R07 items Nick left open (paw kept by his ruling).
Front and side: four near-equal toe lobes in a straight row with straight cone claws on the toe fronts, and a vertical heel face with no domed instep (posed foot band IoU .642).
Front: the knee is a lit band over an inner crease instead of a soft kneecap plane, and the posed thigh and shin bands miss the sheet (IoU .828 and .644).
